**The "Porinju effect" and regulatory record**
- Commentary notes that his small-cap bulk-deal buys often trigger days of upper circuits as retail investors pile in. One critic suggests his "shotgun" spread of bulk deals exploits this excitement. This is opinion, not a finding — [blog](https://rakesh-jhunjhunwala.in/why-is-porinju-veliyath-buying-so-many-stocks-if-he-is-a-concentrated-portfolio-investor/). Business Standard reported that BEML rose 51% in five weeks after his firm bought a stake — [Business Standard topic page](https://www.business-standard.com/topic/porinju-veliyath)
- The only SEBI order I found naming him is a consent/settlement order dated 11 Sep 2009, "in the matter of Geojit Securities Limited". The terms and allegations were not visible on the page — [SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/enforcement/orders/sep-2009/consent-order-on-the-application-submitted-by-shri-porinju-veliyath-in-the-matter-of-geojit-securities-limited_3827.html)
- In 2018 SEBI began a general preliminary probe into the sharp mid/small-cap fall, seeking details of bulk traders. No reporting ties him to it — [Business Standard, Jul 2018](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/sebi-probes-sharp-fall-in-the-midcap-stocks-amid-unfair-trade-allegations-118072301145_1.html)
